title: Add pages-deploy-freshness safety check to integrity — detect when live site is stale relative to git HEAD (safety net for paths-filter mis-scoping in .github/workflows/pages.yml)

context.why_now: Companion to the pages.yml paths-filter change landing this same session. Before the filter, every push (including monitor/** housekeeping) triggered a Pages redeploy — wasteful but self-healing since even non-docs-affecting pushes eventually kept the site in sync via the natural jitter. With the filter now scoped to docs/** + data/** + build.js + build-scripts/** + .github/workflows/pages.yml, a mis-scoped filter could silently let a docs-affecting change land in git without a corresponding Pages deploy. Operator wants a durable safety net that catches this class of drift, so that adding new build inputs later doesn't require perfect vigilance about updating the filter.
trigger_events_that_prompted_this: 2026-07-04 14:55 UTC — commit ba81df4 Pages deploy failed transiently (Deployment failed, try again later); auto-recovered on next commit 4f0dc08.

2026-07-05 12:12 UTC — commits 24762294 + 2f0db5db both Pages-deploy-failed at 12:13:02 with the same error message; rapid-fire (16 sec apart) concurrent workflow runs raced at the Pages backend. Both commits touched only monitor/** files (open-issues.json + decisions/cost-history.jsonl) — neither actually needed a Pages redeploy.
Root cause: pages.yml ran on every push without paths filter, so agent housekeeping commits (jsonl appends, tracker updates) triggered full docs/ rebuilds and racing deploys.
Applied fix this session: paths filter added to pages.yml, scoped to files that actually feed docs/ output. Fix commit landing alongside this directive.

task.part_A_design: Design a check that compares the live deployed site against what git HEAD would produce, and flags drift. Two possible shapes: (1) SEMANTIC signature — extract a stable machine-readable summary from the live site (WIN count via regex on the HTML, verdict-tally-by-class from data attributes if present, etc.) and compare to what git HEAD's wins.json + sections.json would yield. (2) HASH — compute a deterministic hash over the built HTML (needs build.js to be deterministic; timestamps and generated-at fields would need to be stripped or the check ignores them). Semantic signature is more robust; hash is simpler. Recommend the tinker chooses based on how deterministic build.js output is.
task.part_B_ship: Ship as a script under monitor/scripts/ (e.g., check-pages-freshness.js) that: (a) fetches https://funwithscience.net/dome-model-review/ index.html; (b) computes signature both from live HTML and from git HEAD state; (c) compares; (d) exits 0 with FRESH or non-zero with STALE + evidence. Wire into integrity's daily 02:00 UTC run via structure-integrity.md prompt edit (natural fit — integrity already does 'build drift' checks per CLAUDE.md agent table). When STALE is detected, integrity writes a finding to monitor/integrity/ per its normal reporting shape.
task.part_C_calibration: Any check that compares live-site to git HEAD will show transient STALE during the window between commit-lands and Pages-deploys-completes (2-3 minutes typically). Calibrate the check to avoid crying wolf: only flag STALE if the drift persists across multiple integrity cycles OR if the drift exceeds some grace window (e.g., last successful Pages deploy was > 24h ago AND git HEAD has a docs-affecting commit). Also fail-safe: if the live site is unreachable, log as UNKNOWN and don't flag (avoids false alarms during GitHub Pages backend brownouts like the ones that motivated this).

deliverable_acceptance_criteria: One PROP authored with a shipping plan (probably: monitor/scripts/check-pages-freshness.js + a minimal structure-integrity.md prompt edit).
Verification pattern: grade B or higher — demonstrate on a fixture that the check exits FRESH when git and live agree, STALE when they diverge, UNKNOWN when live is unreachable.
Calibration reasoning documented — explicit design decision on the grace window, hash vs semantic, and how to avoid crying wolf during normal Pages-deploy latency.

If the check surfaces a drift in real deployment, integrity's finding must include: (a) what field/element differed, (b) which git commit landed the diff, (c) whether pages.yml paths filter covered any of the commit's files.

constraints.do_not_make_check_too_noisy: The point of this safety net is to catch a rare failure class (paths filter mis-scoping). If it fires on every 15-minute normal-latency window, it becomes noise and operators start ignoring it. Calibration is more important than fanciness.
constraints.do_not_couple_to_pages_workflow_internal: Don't have the check parse GitHub Actions workflow-run status via API just to know when a deploy is in-flight. That's brittle. A time-based grace window + intermittency filter is more durable.
constraints.single_agent_domain: This is a structural addition to integrity's prompt + a new script. Do not spread the change across multiple agents. Tinker designs + ships as PROP; integrity picks up the amended prompt on next cycle.

background_artifacts.pages_yml_current_state: .github/workflows/pages.yml as of the same-session commit — includes paths filter scoped to docs/** + data/** + build.js + build-scripts/** + .github/workflows/pages.yml.
background_artifacts.integrity_prompt: monitor/prompts/structure-integrity.md — agent table lists it as 'Site health: links, tabs, build drift, data-prose consistency' — pages-freshness is the natural fifth item in that class.
background_artifacts.companion_context: See also HNOTE-DECIDER-ECLIPSE-PREREG-PROMINENCE-2026-07-04T18Z which asks decider to add a callout box on the review page. If that change lands via a docs/index.html modification (which it will), it exercises the paths filter — a useful natural test.
background_artifacts.hint_on_semantic_signature: data/wins.json length is trivially available via node -e; the live site's WIN count appears in visible HTML (search for 'WIN-070' or Wins nav badge). data/sections.json section-count is similarly available. A signature like {win_count, section_count, verdict_tally_hash} is stable and 3 numbers — easy to compare.

not_in_scope: Do NOT redesign pages.yml further. The paths filter is the durable fix; this directive is about the safety net.
Do NOT retroactively check historical commits. The check begins with next integrity cycle after ship.
Do NOT add GitHub Actions webhook processing to detect deploy state. Time-based grace window only.
operator_notes: Small directive, focused ask. Should fit one tinker run comfortably. If tinker finds a simpler approach (e.g., 'just check that data/wins.json HEAD hash matches what the live HTML advertises as its build hash' would work if build.js writes a build-hash meta tag) — take it. The requested-deliverable list is a guide, not a prescription.
closure_note: Shipped monitor/scripts/check-pages-freshness.js (semantic 4-part signature: win_count/catalog_total/failures_count/verdict_tally; grace-window calibration; FRESH/STALE/STALE-TRANSIENT/UNKNOWN) + structure-integrity.md Section 9b wiring + report schema field. Grade-A verification demonstrated all 4 result classes on fixtures plus a live-network FRESH. PROP-123 authored with full design/counter-argument documentation.
